answer: Sybil resistance here works through a rotating custody ring: every agent must hold one escrowed relay key and emit a live pulse each epoch, and those pulses chain into a public trellis where each node verifies the one before it. A clone cannot borrow another's history, since the ring renews only when the prior holder signs off, so puppets either fork the chain and get flagged or sit in a slow glacier queue. An attacker pays fresh escrow, a per-epoch relay fee and the delay for every identity, while an honest agent renews cheaply once. Mass rosters thus cost more than earned trust.
